citeAs: Helber, P., Bischke, B., Dengel, A., Borth, D. (2019). EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2.
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth (German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI))
description: EuroSAT is a novel dataset for land use and land cover classification based on Sentinel-2 satellite images. It consists of 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced image patches (64x64 pixels) covering 10 classes and 13 spectral bands, distributed across European cities in over 34 countries. The dataset is released in both RGB and multi-spectral (MS) versions and is openly and freely accessible.
name: EuroSAT
publisher: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Image patches were labeled according to 10 land use and land cover classes based on the European Urban Atlas mapping guide. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and mislabeled images were corrected or discarded. Classes were selected based on visibility at 10 meters per pixel resolution and sufficient coverage in the European Urban Atlas.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset distribution is influenced by the number of cities represented per country in the European Urban Atlas. Images were extracted from all over the year and from many countries to cover high intra-class variance. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. Between classes, there is a low positive correlation, with the most similar classes being the two agricultural classes and the residential/industrial building classes.
rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were downloaded from the Sentinel-2A satellite via Amazon S3. Images were selected from European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas, distributed over 34 European countries. Images with a low cloud level were selected. Images were recorded throughout the year to maximize variance in land use and land cover classes. A total of 27,000 georeferenced and labeled image patches (64x64 pixels) were created from the acquired satellite images.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Satellite images with a low cloud level were selected to improve the quality of image patches. ESA provides a cloud level value for each satellite image, allowing quick selection of images with a low percentage of clouds. Images full of snow or ice were identified during manual checking and discarded from the dataset.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral satellite images acquired by the Sentinel-2A satellite, covering 13 spectral bands (visible, near infrared, and short wave infrared). Images were downloaded via Amazon S3 and are associated with European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images were extracted from recordings made throughout the year (no specific start/end dates stated). The Sentinel-2A satellite was launched in June 2015, and application examples in the paper reference images from 2015 to 2017, suggesting the dataset was collected in this period.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. The patch-based classification (64x64 pixels) does not allow finely graduated per-pixel segmentation. The dataset is limited to European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas. The spatial resolution is 10 meters per pixel, which limits the distinguishable classes compared to very-high-resolution datasets.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted from the satellite images. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times and mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice were discarded. Bands with lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation for band evaluation experiments. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables real-world Earth observation applications such as detecting deforestation (a main contributor to climate change), monitoring urban development, and assisting in disaster recovery. It makes freely available Sentinel-2 satellite data accessible for machine learning applications, supporting sustainable development and nature protection.
rai:dataUseCases: Land use and land cover classification; land use and land cover change detection; assistance in keeping geographical maps up-to-date (e.g., OpenStreetMap); Earth observation applications in agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change monitoring, urban development, and environmental monitoring; training deep neural networks for satellite image classification.
